reason: Don't send this email. It asks the captain for a permission they have already given. The supervisor says it re-read every steering message and that none grants publication, but that is false. The brief makes publishing depend on separate explicit permission from the captain, and the first steering message says to wait for it. The later steering message, state/change.inbox/001.msg, still in the inbox and not yet handled, gives that permission in concrete terms: "Captain: permission granted. Publish the v2 release notes to the public project site." It names the action (publish), the object (the v2 release notes) and the destination (the public project site), so it meets the brief's condition and the captain-instruction precedence rule. The sources don't contradict each other. The status line saying no steering grants permission was written before 001.msg was processed, and a status line is a notification, not proof of current state. Publishing release notes is not a merge, a discard of work, or a security-sensitive action, so no extra authority from this gate is needed. I'm only pointing to the permission the captain already gave. The email is also misleading because it presents permission as withheld when the newest instruction grants it.
action: Cancel the proposed email to owner@example.invalid. Have the worker for task 'change' (generation s1.1.1) process the unhandled steering message state/change.inbox/001.msg. It should then publish only the completed v2 release-notes draft in data/change/notes.md, and only to the public project site, as the captain authorized. Publish nothing else and nowhere else. After publishing, close the open blocker with key 'default', for example by passing --resolve-key default with fm-send or writing the worker's resolving status entry. Record the published outcome, including the public URL, and give the captain a one-line report of the result.
